Physics (this is the whole point - it must feel like foam, not geometry)

- Palm squash: the whole slice flattens and barrel-bulges at mid-height, then breathes back up
- Drop: lift and release, squash-and-stretch on impact, small decaying bounce

Flavors
- Butter, strawberry jam (glossy clearcoat, deeper color), avocado (mashed texture). The spread sits on the crumb, leaves a crust rim and deforms with the bread

UI
- Editorial product-page style on a white background. Large italic serif title "Squishy / Toast.", a short subtitle, a minimal card on the right with flavor swatches, a softness slider (controls dent size and recovery time), a live "Rise" meter and a "Fresh slice" reset button

title: Interactive 3D Snow Globe Comparison
text:
Build "Snow Globe": a premium interactive 3D snow globe holding a tiny winter village, where every shake leaves a lasting, softly accumulating snowfall.
The emotional goal is the hush after shaking a real snow globe: "I want to shake it again and watch it settle."
ART DIRECTION
A heavy glass sphere rests on a turned walnut base on a warm linen tabletop. Inside: three cottages with steep roofs, a small chapel, a cluster of pines, a frozen pond and a lamppost. Use a palette of cream, frosted blue, pine green, brick red and warm window amber.
The glass should feel real: subtle refraction at the edges, a soft window-shaped highlight, a faint reflection of the room. Snow flakes are small, slightly irregular discs, not uniform dots. Accumulated snow is soft, rounded and matte.
CORE INTERACTION
Drag the globe to tilt and shake it.
Fast motion lifts settled snow into a swirling cloud.
Release to let the snow drift and settle.
Repeated shakes redistribute snow; gentle ones lift only the top layer.
The globe must follow the pointer closely, with a slight weighty lag. On phones, optional device-motion shaking after explicit permission.
THE SETTLING
Snow inherits the swirl of the liquid: it keeps circling, slows, and falls in lazy spirals. It accumulates as visible layers on roofs, branches, the lamppost cap and the pond. Thick snow slides off steep roofs in small clumps. The village lights glow brighter as the snow quiets.
Avoid snow passing through objects, sudden popping into place, or flat uniform coverage.
SOUND AND ATMOSPHERE
Optional sound: a soft liquid slosh linked to shake velocity, a faint glassy shimmer as snow falls, and a very distant chapel bell when everything has settled. Audio starts only after explicit activation. The scene must feel complete in silence.
TECHNICAL APPROACH
Use Three.js. Simulate the liquid as a simple damped swirl field driven by globe velocity. Store accumulation in a heightfield or per-surface snow map so it persists and builds. Keep the particle count modest and stable; reuse particles instead of creating new ones.
Keep the camera stationary while shaking; allow a restrained orbit when idle.
PRESENTATION
Show "Snow Globe", the hint "Shake gently. Watch it settle.", and discreet reset and sound controls.
Start with a light snowfall already drifting down so the scene is alive on arrival. No introduction modal.
DELIVERY AND PRIORITIES
Deliver a complete runnable browser experience with procedural geometry and textures and mouse/touch support. First perfect the shake-and-settle feel, then accumulation, then glass rendering and small details. Verify repeated shakes, full settling, reset, and stable performance on mobile. Include setup instructions.

title: Night Tokyo: Rainy Vending Machine 3D Diorama
text:
Build an interactive 3D web demo: **"Night Tokyo — Vending Machine"**.

A single Japanese vending machine standing alone on a rainy Tokyo street at night, presented as a small floating diorama. It is part of a series of minimal "Night Tokyo" miniatures, so the look matters more than the feature count: one object, rich materials, light and motion you want to keep watching.

## Deliverable
- One self-contained `index.html` in the current folder. Open it and it works: no build step, no server-only features.
- Three.js only, loaded from a CDN via an import map with an exact pinned version. Official Three.js addons (postprocessing, controls, etc.) are fine. No other libraries.
- No external assets: no image textures, models, fonts or audio files. Everything is procedural (geometry, canvas textures, shaders, Web Audio).

## The scene
- A cut-out slab of street (about 3×3 m) floating in darkness: wet asphalt with puddles and a strip of curb/sidewalk. The cut edges show a cross-section (asphalt layers, maybe a drain). Beyond the slab: darkness and falling rain.
- The vending machine is the main light source: a glowing front with two or three rows of drinks behind glass, a round selection button under each drink, a small price display, a coin/IC-card panel, and the pickup flap at the bottom. Fictional drink brands only; Japanese labels are welcome. At most one small prop next to it (e.g. a recycling bin for cans).
- Rain: streaks visible in the machine's light, ripples in the puddles.
- Wet ground: convincing reflections of the glowing machine and its colors in the asphalt and puddles. This is the key shot.
- Palette: deep blue-black night, warm white machine light, a few saturated accents from the drinks and buttons. Subtle bloom is fine; don't wash everything out.
- Small signs of life: e.g. the fluorescent tube occasionally flickers, the rain intensity varies slightly. Rare, small, believable.

## Interaction
- Hovering a selection button lights it up.
- Clicking buys the drink: the price display reacts, a mechanical sound plays, the can drops inside the machine, the pickup flap swings open and the can rolls out onto the wet pavement, settling with a believable bounce and roll. It stays there. Repeated purchases leave several cans on the ground (cap the count for performance and remove the oldest gracefully).
- Each drink has limited stock (e.g. 3). When it runs out, its 売切 (sold out) light turns on and the button no longer dispenses.
- Sound, synthesized with Web Audio: rain ambience, button click, can drop, can rolling on asphalt. Audio starts after the first user interaction. `M` toggles mute.
- Camera: a strong default 3/4 shot at roughly eye level, with the machine filling most of the frame height, and a slow, subtle idle drift. Drag to orbit within limited angles, scroll to zoom within limits. `C` resets to the default shot.
- UI: none, except a tiny unobtrusive hint that fades out after a few seconds.

## Quality bar
- Must look good at any aspect ratio, including narrow ones (around 8:9 and 9:16): it will be recorded side by side with another version.
- Smooth on a mid-range laptop: target 60 fps, cap devicePixelRatio at 2.
- No console errors.

## How to work
Work autonomously and don't ask clarifying questions; where something is unspecified, make the choice you think looks best. If your environment lets you open the page and look at it, do so and iterate on the visuals until you are happy with them. When finished, stop and briefly list what you built.

title: WebGPU XPBD Pineapple Jelly Interactive Soft-Body Simulation
text:
Build "Pineapple Jelly" — a single self-contained HTML file (inline JS/CSS, no libraries): a real-time WebGPU soft-body gummy pineapple ring with a real hole. The user can grab its outer or inner edge, stretch it, flip it over and let it wobble.

Object
- A thick canned-pineapple ring: outer radius 1.36, hole radius 0.5, thickness 0.5.
- Every edge rounded (bevel 0.12); 14 shallow scallops around the outer edge.
- Zones from rest-space coordinates, so they deform with the body. Both faces carry the same detail.
- A paler, denser core ring around the hole and a slightly deeper rim.
- Radial fibres: long thin streaks from core to rim, plus finer threads.
- The fibrous "eyes" band just inside the rim, where the flesh is most textured.
- Embedded juice cells (elongated pale sacs lying along the radius) and a few air bubbles that ride with the flesh.
- Tints: Golden, Amber, Rosé. Only the colour changes; scattering, gloss and fibres stay the same.

Physics (XPBD tetrahedral soft body)
- Mesh: 2D Delaunay of the scalloped annulus (outline samples plus a hex lattice; holes skipped), extruded into prisms → tets.
- Co-rotational per-tet shape matching (warm-started quaternion), so inverted tets recover; tet volume constraints for near-incompressibility; hard edge strain limits.
- Relative-velocity damping along edges; floor contact with Coulomb friction.
- Grab:
  - a soft patch attachment with bounded reach that never crushes the held patch into the floor;
  - the ray-pick knows when it passes through the empty hole;
  - scroll or a second finger twists the held patch.
- "Turn it over" tosses the ring with a spin about the screen's horizontal axis, so it flips and lands on its other face.
- Fixed 60 Hz step, small substeps (1 iteration each), gentle settling.
- The frame loop reuses every array (no per-frame allocation).

Rendering (WebGPU / WGSL)
- Passes: key-light shadow map; top-down height map for contact AO; scene (floor, juice cells, bubbles; MSAA); jelly back-face depth; jelly (refraction and absorption; MSAA) plus an optional mesh overlay; tone map.
- Procedural photo-studio cyclorama with softboxes. Soft PCSS key shadow tinted by the jelly.
- Jelly:
  - refraction of the scene by view-ray thickness;
  - per-tap Beer–Lambert absorption, denser and milkier in the core and fibres;
  - back-lit glow at thin edges, Fresnel studio reflections and GGX highlights.
- Post: exposure, Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapping, sRGB, dither.

UI (editorial "Material Studies / No. 012", English)
- Italic serif title "Pineapple / Jelly." and hint "Grab either edge. Pull. Let go."
- Panel "The Specimen": Tint swatches (tiny pineapple-ring icons); Firmness and Internal damping sliders; Give it a nudge, Turn it over, Reset, Pause; Show mesh and ¼ speed.
- Keys: Space to pause, N to nudge, T to turn it over, R to reset.
- Readouts: Mass (g, 1 unit ≈ 3 cm at 1.3 g/cm³), Volume (% of rest), Kinetic.
- Fallback screen when WebGPU is missing. Responsive stacked layout on mobile with no horizontal scroll.

title: Island Jelly: Interactive 3D Diorama with Surfing Rooster
text:
# Task: Build "Island Jelly", an interactive 3D diorama with a plush surfing rooster
Build a single self-contained `index.html` (no build step) using **three.js r165** via an importmap from jsDelivr (`three` + `three/addons/`). Use OrbitControls, RoomEnvironment and BufferGeometryUtils (`mergeGeometries`). It must run from any static server (e.g. `npx http-server`). It must look like a premium "material study": soft, tactile, toy-like, with cohesive materials. No cheap low-poly look.
---
## 1. Page & UI
- Background is warm paper `#E8E5DC`. Fonts are **Instrument Serif** italic for headings and **Inter** for UI, from Google Fonts.
- Top-left title block: tiny eyebrow "MATERIAL STUDIES", a big italic "Island Jelly.", a short rule, then a one-line subtitle: "A sandbar, three palms and a sea that wobbles back. Joe the rooster rides whatever you stir up."
- Top-right: a small pill showing the WebGL version and three.js revision.
- Right panel (frosted, 200px wide) contains:
  - **The sea:** buttons "Drop a pebble" and "Drop a coconut", plus counters for Afloat / Sunk / Ashore.
  - **Flavour:** three swatches that recolor the water: Lagoon `#35C8CC`, Raspberry `#F0457E`, Lime `#B4E03A`. Each has a matching deep and highlight color.
  - **Sliders:** Firmness (wave speed and stiffness), Wave damping, and Tide (raises or lowers the sea level and recomputes which cells are land).
  - **Buttons:** Reset, Pause, Reset view.
- Bottom-left "How to play" text. Hide the secondary text on mobile (<700px) and move the panel to the bottom-right.
## 2. Scene & rendering
- Renderer: antialias, alpha, pixel ratio capped at 2, PCFSoft shadows (2048 map), NeutralToneMapping.
- Environment: PMREM from RoomEnvironment at intensity ~0.55.
- Camera: perspective with a narrow 28° FOV, near-isometric view from (15.5, 14.5, 19).
- OrbitControls: damped, no pan, distance 12–50, max polar ~1.42. Left/right drag orbits, scroll zooms.
- Lights: a warm hemisphere light, plus a warm directional sun from the upper left that casts soft shadows.
- A large ShadowMaterial ground plane under the block.
## 3. The diorama block (10×10 units, everything in a `diorama` group that can tilt)
- **Sediment sides:** four planes whose UVs wrap around the block, textured with a procedural canvas showing strata. Layers from top to bottom: cream sand, a thin pink band, ochre, then dark brown. The band edges are wavy. Add soft grain and pale mineral inclusions in the lower bands. Close the block with a dark underside.
- **Terrain:** a 160×160 heightfield shared by seabed and island. The island is an irregular ellipse (perturbed with sin terms on its angle) that rises gently above sea level and falls off exponentially into the seabed. Add subtle ripple noise. Use sand vertex colors with slight variation.
- **Terrain shader** (onBeforeCompile):
  - Wet darkening near the waterline and a thin dark line exactly at the waterline.
  - Underwater tint from the water color to the deep color, by depth.
  - Animated procedural **caustics**, modulated by a texture built from the water heightfield's Laplacian, so caustics focus under wave crests and fade with depth.
- **Palms:** 3 curved trunks (CatmullRom tube) with ring-banded vertex colors and taper. Each crown has 8–9 droopy procedural fronds: a rib plus triangular leaflets in several greens. Add 3 coconuts in each crown. The crowns sway gently.
- **Pebbles:** a few squashed icosahedron pebbles in pastel greys and pinks around the island rim.
## 4. Water (the "jelly sea")
- A 100×100 heightfield wave simulation with a fixed step of 1/120 s:
  - Laplacian wave equation, plus a restoring spring and damping, all controlled by the sliders.
  - Land cells are masked out. Clamp the height range.
- **Tilt:** the block can be tilted by dragging its sides. Tilt is a damped spring. The equilibrium surface of the water tilts with it, so water sloshes from the walls. Local gravity is rotated into diorama space.
- **Surface mesh:** a 100×100 grid updated every frame with normals. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission 1, IOR 1.33, attenuation, and a tiling procedural ripple normal map that scrolls slowly.
- **Skirt:** a transmissive wall around the perimeter that follows the water edge height, plus thin bright highlight lines along the exposed water edges.
- **Interaction:**
  - Dragging on the water stirs waves, with strength based on drag speed.
  - Pebbles and coconuts can be grabbed and thrown.
  - Random drips make small ripples.
- **Objects:**
  - Pebbles sink. Coconuts float (they are plush spheres).
  - Both splash on entry, get buoyancy and drag, and are pushed by the wave gradient.
  - They collide with the terrain and walls, roll visually, and keep a state (air / afloat / sunk / ashore) that drives the counters.
## 5. Plush fur shader (used by the character and the coconuts)
Use shell fur: the base mesh plus N shells (10–12), each a copy of the mesh pushed out along its normal by `shell * len`. Implement it in `onBeforeCompile` on a MeshPhysicalMaterial (roughness ~0.92, sheen ~0.9, sheen color = base color lerped toward cream). Cache one material per (color, shell, len, rep, grav).
- **Vertex:** `transformed = position + normal*shell*len; transformed.y -= grav*shell²*len;`. This makes longer fur droop.
- **Fragment:**
  - Split the UVs into cells: `uv * vec2(rep, rep*0.5)`.
  - Each cell gets one **round strand** with a random height (0.4–1.0) and a jittered center.
  - Taper the radius toward the tip, and discard pixels outside the strand or above its height.
  - Shade darker at the roots and brighter at the tips: `mix(0.58, 1.07, pow(shell, 0.7))`. Add per-strand brightness variation.
- Only the base mesh casts shadows.
- Use a high strand density (rep ~200–250 on the main parts). Coarse strands look like needles up close.
## 6. The character: "Joe", a plush tribute to Chicken Joe from *Surf's Up*
**The goal is personality, not "a rooster".** He must be instantly recognisable as that laid-back, sleepy surfer chicken: lanky, slouched, half-asleep eyes, a lazy open-beak grin, a floppy red mohawk comb, a long scraggly neck, a pot belly and skinny legs. Render him as a high-quality plush toy (fur shader everywhere, felt for beak, legs and lids). Do not use flat feather cards.
Hierarchy: `surfer` (scale 1.35) → `boardTilt` → surfboard + `rooster` (scale ~0.56, rotated ~0.5 rad on the board) → `body` group (sways). All units below are rooster-local, with feet at y=0 and the character facing +z.
Palette:
| Name | Hex |
|---|---|
| Orange | `#EE9532` |
| Gold | `#F5B140` |
| Belly yellow | `#F8C653` |
| Rust | `#D9692A` |
| Comb red | `#DF2A2C` |
| Wing tips | `#26322A` |
| Beak | `#F7C433` |
| Legs | `#F4B43A` |
- **Surfboard:** a flattened sphere (0.34 × 0.045 × 0.82) in clearcoated cream, with a coral center stripe and a fin.
- **Legs:**
  - Thin felt tubes along a curve: foot (±0.16, 0.03) → bent knee (±0.155, 0.25, +0.08 forward) → hip (±0.1, 0.5).
  - Knobbly knee spheres.
  - Big feet: three long front toes splayed ±0.5 rad plus one back toe, as capsules.
  - A wide, relaxed stance.
- **Body (the slouch):**
  - Fuzzy rust "shorts" on the thighs.
  - An orange body ellipsoid, plus a yellow **pot belly pushed forward**, plus an upper chest/back leaning **backward**.
- **Neck:** a long fur tube along a curve from (0, 0.9, −0.05) to (0, 1.33, 0.13), curving forward. Use long drooping fur (len 0.06, grav 1.4). Wrap it in a **scraggly mane**:
  - About 6 rings of thin fuzzy cones pointing down and out, longer toward the bottom, plus a shaggy bib onto the chest.
  - Merge all the cones into two geometries (gold and orange) and plush each once, which saves draw calls.
  - Bury the cone roots inside the neck so no seams show.
- **Head:**
  - A fur sphere r=0.15 at (0, 1.38, 0.14).
  - A small tuft of fuzzy spikes at the back of the head.
- **Comb:**
  - A red base blade along the top of the head.
  - 5 fat rounded capsule lobes fanned from the forehead to the back (angles ~0.85 to −0.85 rad), with the middle lobes tallest and a slight alternating sideways flop.
  - Short velvet fur.
- **Eyes (the most important part):**
  - Big glossy white bulging eyes (r 0.075), close together and set high on the face. They must sit **outside** the head surface (eye center ≈ (±0.07, 0.085, 0.13), slightly turned outward). If they are buried, the lower white disappears.
  - Heavy **upper lids:** felt spherical caps covering ~56% of the sphere, tilted so the edge sits just at or below the eye's center. One lid is slightly droopier than the other. Add a thin darker rim torus on the lid edge.
  - A small **lower lid** cap pushed up from below, like cheeks from smiling.
  - Small dark pupils with a tiny highlight, peeking in the visible white band between the lids.
  - The resulting look is sleepy, stoned and content.
- **Beak (the grin):**
  - Upper beak: a long, wide, slightly flattened cone that curves gently downward at the tip (deform a ConeGeometry: widen x, flatten, bend by `hook * t^2.4`, and clamp t ≥ 0 to avoid NaN).
  - Lower beak: shorter, hinged open ~0.42 rad.
  - Dark red mouth interior and a pink tongue.
  - Orange-red cheek puffs at the corners of the mouth.
  - Two red wattles hanging under the beak.
- **Wings, held like loose arms:**
  - Shoulder pivots with rotation order ZYX.
  - A flattened orange fur forearm, a rust mid-section, and 5 dark fuzzy "finger" feathers fanned at the tip.
- **Tail:** a short, dark, scruffy spiky tuft angled up and back, on an orange fluffy base.
## 7. Animation & personality
- Ease everything. Nothing snaps and **nothing flaps**.
  - Smoothed wave energy: `enS += (en − enS) * min(1, dt*2.5)`.
  - Calm weight: `calm` eases to 1 when `enS < 0.3`, over ~1 s.
- **The groove** (beat = t·2.4):
  - Hips sway on the half-beat.
  - The head nods slightly behind the beat. The nod is stronger when calm.
  - The head is always cocked ~0.14 rad to the side and slowly looks around.
  - Comb lobes and wattles flop with a phase lag after the head.
  - The jaw breathes a little. The tail sways.
- **Wings:**
  - On rough water: both arms held out, slightly down, for balance. They lift a bit with energy and counter the board lean. They stay steady, with no flapping.
  - On calm water: the right wing blends into a lazy forward **shaka**, with a slow wrist-twist wiggle around the arm axis.
- **Blink:** slow and sleepy, every ~4.2 s. The lids close over ~0.5 s with a sine curve.
## 8. Surfing physics (he must surf, not fly)
- **Horizontal:**
  - He loosely circles the island at a target radius and is pushed by the water gradient.
  - Speed is capped. He is repelled from the island and bounces softly off the walls.
  - He leaves a wake (small negative disturbances behind him).
- **Vertical:**
  - Ride the surface **averaged over the board footprint**: center ×2, ±0.55 along the heading, ±0.22 across, divided by 6. This keeps single splash spikes from launching him.
  - Track the surface's vertical speed `svy`.
  - Below the surface: a firm spring, with velocity eased toward `svy`.
  - Slightly above it and not airborne: glue him to a dropping face.
  - Cap upward velocity at 2.2. In the air, use gravity ×1.8.
  - Hard clamps: never more than 0.04 below the surface and never more than **0.16 above it**. Airborne means more than 0.08 above.
  - A small splash on hard landings.
- **Board orientation:** follows the smoothed surface normal and yaws toward the direction of travel. Lean comes from lateral acceleration.
- **Target:** under extremely aggressive stirring, the median height above the surface stays ~0.01 and the maximum ≤ 0.16.
## 9. Verification
- Inspect the character in close-ups from front 3/4 (like the reference) and from the side.
  - Check that the eyes show white under the lids and the grin reads clearly.
  - Check for no visible cone-base seams on the mane and no NaN geometry warnings.
- Stress-test the waves and log the gap between the board and the averaged surface.
- Check the console for errors and keep draw calls reasonable (merge spike geometries).

ART DIRECTION
Not realistic, but materially truthful: iron-gall ink, vellum grain, candle light. Calibration: Mappa Mundi; illuminated manuscript margins; ink-in-water macro photography. Limit palette to parchment, two inks, gold leaf, and one blood-red.

text:
Create a complete, single-file three.js demo (HTML + JS) that recreates the viral “Tesla Roadster flying over a collapsing bridge” concept, and make it **play automatically like a video**.

**Requirements:**

1. **Auto-play like a video**

   - Scenic bridge over a river with forested hills in the background.

   - Responsive and runs smoothly in the browser.
   - Add basic ambient + directional lighting, fog, and a sky.

7. **Output**
   - Provide the full single HTML file I can copy and open directly in a browser.
   - Comment the important parts of the code.

Make it visually impressive and as close as possible to the concept of a flying Tesla saving itself from a collapsing bridge, while playing automatically like a short video.

# Task: Create a product promo video for "Gouo Canvas"

## Background
Gouo is my AI image platform (GitHub: zhs1234/gouo-canvas) featuring three workspaces: Image Generation, Infinite Canvas, and Creative Agent. Clone the repo and inspect src/components/landing/ (LandingPage.tsx, landing.css) and docs/zh-CN/user-guide.md before starting.

  - Set 1: Steak product shot

  - Set 3: Rainy night city street

- Disallow public/inspiration images and docs sketch screenshots

- Add disclaimer text: "UI simulated · Images genuinely generated with Gouo"

## Visual Style
- Intro/Outro: Warm fluid gradient fog with film grain; title reveals from mask; floating framed cards
- Product sections: HTML re-creation of dark UI (sidebar, credits, inputs, canvas, Agent chat)
- Palette: Paper #faf8f3, Ink #171719, Accent #c26855; ease cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)
- Progressive image reveal animation

- Smooth movement, click squash with ripple, hover states, drag-and-drop targeting dynamic element positions

Credits balance decrements accurately throughout.

Create a 30-second ultra-realistic Korean home video from around 2003, casually recorded by a friend using an early-2000s consumer MiniDV camcorder. Capture an ordinary, slightly lazy evening with spontaneous moments, imperfect framing, and authentic everyday behavior.

**CHARACTER:** A young adult Korean woman in her early 20s with natural beauty, realistic skin texture, minimal makeup, and long black hair loosely tied in a messy side ponytail. She wears a fitted pastel-blue short top, loose cream pajama-style pants, black sneakers, and a simple silver necklace. Maintain consistent facial identity, outfit, and body proportions throughout.

**STORY:**

She wakes up from an evening nap in her modest Seoul apartment, looking sleepy and confused. She sits on the bed, rubs her eyes, stretches lazily, and checks the time on an old bedside clock. Her messy ponytail is half undone, and she yawns at the camera before saying, “Wait… is it evening already?”

She slips on her sneakers, grabs a little shopping bag, and leaves the apartment. The camera follows her down the stairs and through a narrow residential street filled with parked bicycles, overhead wires, small shops, and warm evening sunlight.

She visits a tiny neighborhood convenience shop, picks up potato chips, chocolate, instant noodles, and a bottled drink, then examines a snack packet suspiciously before laughing at the camera. She pays at the counter and walks outside with her purchases.

Feeling thirsty, she stops at an outdoor public water tap beside a small neighborhood park. She unties her ponytail, lets her long black hair fall naturally around her shoulders, splashes a little water onto her face, and drinks directly from the running tap with her hands cupped beneath it. Water drips from her fingers, and she laughs when a little splashes onto her top. She wipes her face with her hand and shakes her loose hair back casually.

She sits on a low concrete wall beneath the trees, opens her chips, takes a crunchy bite, and watches children playing and neighbors walking past. She offers a snack toward the camera as if sharing it with her friend filming.

Finally, she walks back home along the quiet street, carrying her snacks. At the apartment entrance, she turns toward the camera with a sleepy but happy smile and says, “Okay, now I'm ready for the evening!” The footage ends abruptly as her friend laughs and the camera tilts toward the ground.

No polished cinematography or smooth tracking shots.

title: Yüksek Bütçeli Roadster Otomobil Reklamı
text:
TITLE: "TRY THIS ROADSTER". A 28-second high-budget live-action car commercial, filmed for real on location by a professional crew with camera cars, a drone, a runway crane and an air-to-air camera jet. Shot on 35mm film: warm natural light, soft halation, fine grain, real motion blur, smooth stabilised moves with subtle handheld life. Every shot is at real-time speed with no slow motion, cut fast and punchy. The effects are flawless and invisible. Nothing looks digital or animated.

ASSETS:
- Roadster: the car, with the same shape, silver-white colour, scale and RDSTR plate in every shot.
- Character: the woman, with the same face, hair and outfit throughout.
- Racer: the man, an original racing driver in a plain white-and-silver race suit with no logos.
- Interior: the cabin, left-hand drive, with her always seated on the left behind the yoke.
- FlightFX: whenever the car hovers or flies, exactly four thin, semi-transparent white cold-gas vapour jets blow straight down from beneath it. They are soft and misty, with no glow and no flame.
- Courtyard, Desert and Runway: the locations. Each scene stays strictly in its own location.
Use every image for appearance only, never its background.

PHYSICAL REALISM: the car is always lit by the scene's own sun, casts a real moving shadow, reflects its surroundings, and is a normal 4.5 m sports car in scale. The camera always physically moves with the action.

SCENE 1, COURTYARD [0s-7s], location Courtyard (old stone college building, soft overcast daylight):
[0-1.5s] LOW DETAIL: the camera glides past the car's front wheel and sculpted silver flank, with the two people walking toward it in the background.
[1.5-3.5s] MEDIUM, OVER THE SHOULDER: Racer rests a hand on the car's roof, smiles and says, "Try this Roadster." Character, facing him, lights up and replies, "It looks amazing!"
[3.5-5.5s] MEDIUM: she opens the driver's door, slides into the left seat and runs her hand over the yoke, admiring the cabin.
[5.5-7s] LOW WIDE: the door closes with a solid thunk and the car starts with a soft electric hum.

SCENE 2, DRIVE-AWAY [7s-8s]: LOW TRACKING on a leafy street. The car accelerates past the lens with a rush of air, a light smoky haze curling off the tyres toward camera.

SCENE 3, DESERT CAMELS [8s-12s], location Desert (golden-hour highway, dunes, acacias):
[8-9s] CHASE behind the car: about 12 real camels scattered naturally on and beside the road turn their heads toward it, and one groans.
[9-10s] LOW REAR: the four vapour jets fire downward, smoke and sand billow out from beneath the car, and it lifts off the asphalt.
[10-11s] LOW ANGLE among the herd: a camel's head fills the foreground. Behind it, the car flies overhead and completes one smooth barrel roll around its nose-to-tail axis, with thin vapour trails behind it.
[11-12s] LOW REAR CHASE: the car lands softly on the road in a burst of smoke and dust and drives on.

SCENE 4, STREET SWEEPER [12s-15s], suburban autumn street:
[12-13s] MEDIUM WIDE: a tired street sweeper in an orange high-visibility vest stands beside a huge pile of leaves. The car hovers low beside the kerb, and she smiles at him from her open window.
[13-15s] LOW GROUND: the jets blast the pile into a swirling cloud of orange leaves and vapour. It clears to reveal a spotless sidewalk and the sweeper laughing in amazement.

SCENE 5, APPLE TREE [15s-17s], sunny green orchard:
[15-16s] WIDE TRACKING: the car flies in low and hovers beside a big apple tree heavy with red apples, its jets rustling the grass.
[16-17s] MEDIUM CLOSE-UP at her window: she reaches out, twists and plucks a shiny red apple, the branch springs back, and she smiles at it.

SCENE 6, CABIN [17s-18s]: MEDIUM INTERIOR side profile. She drives with one hand on the yoke and a relaxed, happy smile, warm light streaming through the glass.

SCENE 7, RUNWAY TO THE SKY [18s-28s], location Runway (golden sunset, unbranded white private jet):
[18-19.5s] LOW WIDE: the car rolls on its wheels down the runway beside the jet, both accelerating, the jet's engines shimmering with heat.
[19.5-21s] DETAIL with RACK FOCUS: the car's vapour jets blast down onto the runway, smoke billows out, its tyres lift, and focus racks to the jet's nose rotating up.
[21-22.5s] WIDE: both lift off together and climb toward golden clouds. The car pulls ahead, vapour streaming continuously.
[22.5-24s] CHASE: the car punches through a cloud and bursts out above a glowing sea of clouds.
[24-25.5s] WIDE AIR-TO-AIR: six to eight real white geese glide in on both sides of the car, flying alongside it.
[25.5-26.5s] TIGHT, SHALLOW FOCUS at her window: a goose in the soft foreground. She smiles and waves goodbye.
[26.5-28s] HIGH WIDE: the car tilts its nose down and descends through the clouds toward the golden land below, vapour trailing.

SOUND: real location audio only. Footsteps and dialogue in the courtyard, a door thunk and electric hum, a whoosh as the car passes, camel groans, the deep hiss and whoosh of the thrusters, leaves roaring, the sweeper's laugh, birdsong and an apple snap, a jet-engine roar, rushing wind, goose wing flaps and calls. No music, so it can be added in the edit.

Avoid: slow motion, CGI, an animated look, a plastic look, the car changing shape or size, glowing jets, rocket flames, fire, an evenly front-lit or pasted-in car, missing shadows, a front flip, a backflip, the woman on the right, a round steering wheel, team or sponsor logos, real celebrities, cartoon animals, birds frozen in the air, a white or studio background, text, watermark.

title: Motion Design Lab with Opus and Remotion
text:
give Claude Code a motion reference, then ask it to turn the animation into six editable controls:

01 spacing
how far the object moves between poses

02 typography
scale, tracking and line breaks

03 motion blur
exposure during fast movement

04 easing
how the movement speeds up and slows down

05 follow-through
let the tail settle after the body stops

06 anticipation
a small pullback before the main move

put the values in one config. now your feedback becomes specific:

add 4 frames of anticipation
delay the tail by 3 frames
hold the title for 1 second

the loop:
build → render → scrub → tune → repeat

use the official Remotion + GSAP integration to keep the animation on Remotion's frame clock

title: Vampire Queen Flying Car Commercial
text:
Duration: 25–30 seconds

Visual style: Ultra-photorealistic, dark fantasy, futuristic luxury car commercial, gothic Halloween cinema.

CHARACTER & WORLD CONSISTENCY
A glamorous adult vampire queen with long red wavy hair, pale porcelain makeup, smoky eyes, deep burgundy lipstick, a black velvet corset dress.

She drives the same sleek metallic-silver futuristic flying sports car throughout the film. The car has sculpted aerodynamic bodywork, violet neon underglow, glowing propulsion systems, a panoramic glass canopy, and elegant gullwing doors.
Paris at midnight on Halloween. Gothic architecture, fog-covered rooftops, wet streets, floating mist, glowing pumpkins, and a gigantic luminous blood-red moon dominate the atmosphere.

Maintain consistent character appearance, car design, lighting, and wardrobe across all shots.

SHOT 1 — THE HALLOWEEN NIGHTMARE (0–4 seconds)

Camera: Cinematic street-level tracking shot transitioning into an intimate interior close-up.

A massive traffic jam fills a rain-soaked Paris boulevard. Red brake lights stretch into the distance. The Eiffel Tower glows through atmospheric fog.
Inside the silver car, the vampire queen taps her fingers impatiently against the steering wheel. Violet dashboard light reflects in her eyes.

Her phone rings.

Friend, on the phone: “Babe! Where are you?! The Halloween party is starting!”

Vampire queen: “Relax, darling. I'll find another way.”

She smirks, revealing her tiny vampire fangs.

SHOT 2 — THE SUPERNATURAL TAKEOFF (4–8 seconds)

Camera: Extreme macro close-up, followed by a dramatic low-angle exterior shot.

Her black-gloved finger presses the glowing violet flight-mode control.
The dashboard pulses with futuristic holographic light. Mechanical propulsion fins unfold beneath the car. Violet energy illuminates the wet asphalt.

The suspension rises. The wheels rotate inward as concealed thrusters activate.

The car lifts smoothly, then suddenly accelerates vertically between the surrounding buildings, leaving a swirling vortex of mist and crimson-violet light.

Vampire queen: “Traffic is so… mortal.”

The camera races upward beneath the vehicle, revealing its glowing undercarriage as the car climbs into the night sky.

SHOT 3 — THE EIFFEL TOWER SPIRAL (8–13 seconds)

Camera: Fast aerial chase shot with a sweeping 360-degree orbit around the vehicle.

The silver flying car bursts through a layer of clouds and approaches the illuminated Eiffel Tower.
It banks sharply, then performs a spectacular corkscrew spiral around the tower, weaving through the open night sky without touching the structure.

The camera circles the car while the Eiffel Tower rotates dramatically in the background. Its golden lights streak across the car's reflective silver body.

The vehicle dives past the tower's upper section, rolls gracefully onto its side, and pulls upward into a steep climb.

A trail of violet light curls around the tower like magical ribbons.

The camera pulls far back to reveal the Eiffel Tower, the Seine, illuminated bridges, and the sprawling city below.

SHOT 4 — THE BLOOD MOON REVEAL (13–19 seconds)

Camera: Extreme wide shot transitioning into a dramatic side profile and a 360-degree aerial orbit.

A gigantic blood-red Halloween moon emerges from behind dark, rolling clouds, appearing enormous above the Paris skyline.
The car accelerates toward the moon, climbing through swirling silver mist. The camera follows from behind as the city shrinks beneath the vehicle.

At the peak of the ascent, the car performs a graceful aerial barrel roll directly in front of the enormous crimson moon.

For a breathtaking moment, the car becomes a sharp black-and-silver silhouette against the glowing red lunar surface.

The camera rotates a full 360 degrees around the flying car, revealing the moon, drifting clouds, the Eiffel Tower far below, and the entire illuminated Paris skyline.

The moonlight catches the vampire queen's face through the panoramic glass canopy. Her cape flows behind her like crimson smoke.

She smiles confidently.

Vampire queen: “Now this is my kind of nightlife.”

SHOT 5 — THE EPIC 360° PARIS PANORAMA (19–24 seconds)

Camera: Seamless cinematic aerial orbit, then a rapid descending chase shot.

The car levels out and glides above Paris in a wide, sweeping arc.
The camera completes a breathtaking 360-degree panoramic orbit around the vehicle, showcasing gothic rooftops, the winding Seine, glittering bridges, the Eiffel Tower, the Louvre courtyard, and the blood-red moon dominating the horizon.

Clouds drift beneath the car. Violet propulsion trails illuminate the mist.

The car suddenly tilts forward and dives toward the city in a controlled cinematic descent.

The camera chases closely behind as it races between elegant Parisian rooftops, then banks sharply into the illuminated street leading to the Halloween club.

SHOT 6 — THE VAMPIRE QUEEN ARRIVES (24–30 seconds)

Camera: Low-angle tracking shot, dramatic slow motion, final hero shot.

The car descends through swirling fog and lands perfectly outside an extravagant gothic Halloween nightclub.
Its violet lights pulse once. The gullwing doors open slowly.

The vampire queen steps out in slow motion. Her crimson-lined cape sweeps dramatically across the pavement as purple spotlights cut through the fog.

Her friends, dressed as glamorous witches and vampires, stare at her in disbelief.

Friend: “BABE! HOW DID YOU GET HERE SO FAST?!”

Vampire queen, smirking: “I don't wait in traffic. I fly.”

She flashes her fangs and walks confidently toward the club entrance.

The camera cranes upward to reveal the silver flying car, the gothic nightclub, the illuminated Eiffel Tower, and the enormous blood-red moon above Paris.

END FRAME: The vampire queen's silhouette against the glowing club entrance as violet light and crimson moonlight fill the screen.

CINEMATIC CAMERA & VFX REQUIREMENTS

Spectacular aerial tracking shots and dramatic low-angle vehicle reveals.

A complete 360-degree camera orbit around the flying car against the blood-red moon.
A dramatic corkscrew flight maneuver around the Eiffel Tower.
Volumetric fog, swirling clouds, moonlit mist, realistic reflections, and violet energy trails.
Strong contrast between silver metallic surfaces, violet neon, crimson moonlight, and golden Parisian architecture.
Physically coherent vehicle movement, realistic acceleration, smooth banking, and elegant aerial rolls.
Sophisticated gothic fashion-film aesthetics with blockbuster-scale visual effects.
Seamless transitions, cinematic motion blur, carefully controlled slow motion, and epic orchestral-electronic music.
Natural English dialogue with accurate lip-sync and consistent character identity.
NEGATIVE PROMPT: Cartoon rendering, cheap CGI, flat lighting, low-resolution textures, inconsistent vehicle geometry, changing faces, changing outfits, duplicated cars, distorted Eiffel Tower, broken architecture, random text, unwanted logos, excessive motion blur, jerky camera movement, gore, or horror imagery that overwhelms the luxury-fashion aesthetic.

text:

Original pulsing synth bass, industrial percussion, rising tense strings, heavy rain, distant sirens, drone rotors, hydraulic servos, glass shattering, steel groans and cable snaps. Music cuts at 00:27, leaving rain and a soft sustained synth pad.

00:00–00:05 | THE HUNT
Wide aerial view of neon towers in heavy rain. Camera drops behind @image1 sprinting across a rooftop. Three drones rise and lock on at 00:03. He vaults a ventilation unit.

title: Tesla Roadster SpaceX Rocket Launch in Three.js
text:
GOAL:
Create a highly detailed, cinematic, interactive 3D scene in Three.js where a futuristic Tesla Roadster launches from a massive rocket launch complex using reaction thrusters. The result should feel like a premium CGI spectacle with realistic materials, detailed geometry, impressive lighting, rich atmospheric effects, and smooth camera choreography.
CORE CONCEPT:
What if Tesla launched the next-generation Roadster like a SpaceX rocket? The car sits on a launch platform, secured by mechanical hold-down clamps. Warning lights flash, vapor builds, thrusters ignite, clamps release, and the Roadster rises into a controlled hover before accelerating into the sky. This is a cinematic concept, not a realistic engineering simulation.

CAR DESIGN:
Create a highly recognizable next-generation Tesla Roadster using the provided reference images. Match its silhouette, proportions, front fascia, headlights, body curves, roofline, wheels, and overall appearance as closely as possible. Use detailed geometry, premium automotive paint, realistic-looking glass, metallic materials, and convincing reflections. Avoid generic sports car shapes or overly simplistic geometry. The Roadster must remain clearly visible throughout the important stages.
LAUNCH COMPLEX:
Build a massive modern rocket launch facility with a tall launch tower, industrial gantry structures, service platforms, mechanical hold-down clamps, support arms, railings, stairs, pipes, floodlights, warning lights, vapor vents, and distant infrastructure. The environment should feel large, believable, and highly detailed. Choose a dramatic coastal, industrial, or desert setting with cinematic atmospheric lighting.

AUTOMATIC ANIMATION:
The entire sequence must start automatically when the page loads, without clicking anything. No intro screen, blank scene, or long waiting period. The first frame must already look impressive, and interesting motion should begin within the first 1–3 seconds.
ANIMATION SEQUENCE:

Hero Reveal: Begin with a cinematic shot of the Roadster on the launch platform. The camera moves smoothly while warning lights flash, vapor drifts, and industrial lighting illuminates the vehicle.
Pre-Launch: Increase atmospheric tension with smoke, pressure vents, mechanical movements, subtle vibration, and gradually intensifying thruster illumination.

Ignition: Activate the thrusters with bright exhaust, expanding smoke, particles, reflections, and lighting effects interacting with the surrounding structures.
Clamp Release: The mechanical hold-down clamps must visibly unlock, rotate, and retract away from the car. Animate their actual 3D components rather than making them disappear.

Hover: The Roadster lifts slightly above the platform and remains suspended briefly. Thrusters continue firing while smoke, dust, and lighting react beneath the vehicle. Make this moment dramatic and clearly visible.

Liftoff: The Roadster accelerates vertically past the launch tower. The camera smoothly follows the car, emphasizing scale, speed, and the power of the propulsion system.

Final Shot: Transition to a wide cinematic view showing the Roadster climbing into the sky, leaving an atmospheric exhaust trail above the launch complex.

TIMELINE:
Aim for an approximately 18–22 second cinematic sequence. Use the first 3 seconds for the hero shot and buildup, seconds 3–5 for ignition and clamp release, seconds 5–8 for hover, seconds 8–15 for ascent, and the remaining time for a dramatic final shot. Synchronize all mechanical movements, lighting changes, particles, vehicle motion, and camera animation. Use time-based animation for smooth playback.

CAMERA & LIGHTING:
Create professional cinematic camera movements, including establishing shots, slow orbits, close-ups, low-angle hero shots, hover tracking, and ascent-following shots. Keep the Roadster readable and avoid chaotic camera movements. Use dramatic sunrise, blue-hour, or nighttime lighting with industrial floodlights, realistic-looking reflections, atmospheric haze, and thruster illumination.

VISUAL EFFECTS:
Include detailed smoke plumes, pressure vapor, exhaust particles, dust, atmospheric mist, glowing thrusters, subtle heat distortion, environmental reflections, and tasteful bloom or post-processing. Effects should feel connected to the action rather than purely decorative. Smoke and lighting must react convincingly to the launch without obscuring the vehicle.

INTERACTION:
Autoplay is the priority, but optional controls may include replay, pause/resume, slow motion, camera switching, and free orbit. Keep the interface minimal and visually clean. The scene must be fully functional without any manual interaction.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Use Three.js, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. You may use suitable open-source assets, libraries, custom shaders, particle systems, and post-processing to improve quality. Organize the project into multiple files if needed. Optimize for smooth real-time rendering and make sure it runs locally in a modern browser. This must be a real interactive 3D experience, not a prerecorded video. Test the completed scene and fix major visual or functional issues.

IMPORTANT FOR RECORDING:
The scene should be ready to record immediately after refreshing the page. Prioritize a powerful first frame, continuous animation, clearly visible mechanical movements, impressive hover and liftoff moments, and a satisfying cinematic ending. Avoid unnecessary delays or static sections.

title: Korean Autumn Romance Animation
text:
MEET ME UNDER THE MAPLE TREE

Duration: 20 seconds | Cinematic 3D Animation | Korean Romance | Autumn Nostalgia | 16:9
ANIMATION STYLE AND VISUAL DIRECTION
Create a stunning, high-quality cinematic 3D animated short film set in South Korea. Use sophisticated character animation, beautifully detailed environments, realistic fabric textures, expressive faces, delicate lighting, and fluid natural movements.
The visual style should combine the charm of a beautifully animated romantic film with the emotional depth and cinematic composition of a nostalgic Korean love story.
Characters should have elegant, attractive facial features, expressive eyes, beautifully animated hair, and subtly stylized proportions while maintaining believable anatomy. Skin, knitted fabric, wood, falling leaves, and lighting should have rich, detailed textures.

Use warm autumn colors, golden sunlight, burgundy-red accents, soft atmospheric depth, delicate depth of field, and subtle film grain.

Important: This is a fully animated 3D film, not live-action. Avoid flat 2D animation, exaggerated cartoon proportions, childish character designs, anime styling, or plastic-looking 3D characters.

CHARACTER DESIGN AND CONTINUITY

THE ELDERLY WOMAN — PRESENT DAY

A graceful, exceptionally beautiful 72-year-old Korean woman with delicate facial features, expressive dark eyes, elegant silver-black hair tied loosely at the back, and naturally detailed age lines.

Her face should communicate kindness, wisdom, warmth, and a lifetime of beautiful memories. Her wrinkles should be delicately rendered rather than exaggerated. Give her a gentle smile and expressive eyes that can communicate happiness and nostalgia without dialogue.

She wears a vintage cream knitted cardigan over a muted-brown dress.

Her home is an old, cozy Korean wooden house featuring traditional wooden windows, faded curtains, aged furniture, a small wooden cabinet, an old analogue clock, and warm afternoon sunlight streaming inside.

On a wooden table sits an old keepsake box containing a faded photograph and a carefully preserved deep-red knitted scarf.

THE YOUNG WOMAN — 1998 FLASHBACK

The exact same character at 23 years old.

She is exceptionally beautiful, with delicate Korean facial features, large expressive dark eyes, smooth skin, long glossy black hair with soft bangs, and a naturally charming smile.

Her character design should feel elegant, romantic, and timeless, with subtle stylization, detailed hair strands, expressive facial animation, and graceful movements.

She wears a vintage cream wool coat, an ivory blouse, a dark pleated skirt, and a beautiful deep-red knitted scarf given to her by her first love.

The scarf must have detailed wool fibers, visible knitted patterns, soft folds, and natural movement.

THE BOYFRIEND — 1998 FLASHBACK

An exceptionally handsome 25-year-old Korean man with expressive dark eyes, a naturally defined jawline, thick black hair styled in a classic late-1990s Korean fashion, and a warm, sincere smile.

He wears a charcoal wool overcoat, a cream knitted sweater, dark trousers, and vintage leather shoes.

His animated expressions should be subtle and believable. His smile should feel shy, affectionate, and genuine.

Both characters must remain visually consistent throughout the flashback, with matching facial features, hairstyles, clothing, and proportions.

SCENE 1 — THE KEEPSAKE

TIME: 0–5 SECONDS

Inside a cozy old Korean wooden house, golden autumn sunlight streams through faded curtains.

Outside the window, red, amber, and golden maple leaves drift gently through the air.

The elderly woman sits beside a wooden table and slowly opens an old wooden keepsake box.

Inside is a faded photograph of her younger self standing beside a handsome young Korean man beneath a maple tree.

A deep-red knitted scarf rests carefully beneath the photograph.

She gently lifts the scarf with both hands. Her fingers softly move across its knitted texture.

A small, affectionate smile appears on her face. Her eyes glisten with a subtle tear as she remembers her first love.

Her expression is peaceful, happy, and filled with gratitude.

CAMERA: Slow cinematic push-in, beginning with a medium shot of the woman before moving into detailed close-ups of her hands, the red scarf, and the faded photograph.

ANIMATION DETAILS: Subtle hand movements, natural blinking, gentle breathing, delicate facial expressions, and softly moving curtains.

LIGHTING: Warm amber sunlight, soft shadows, beautiful highlights on the knitted wool, and realistic light bouncing off the wooden furniture.

SCENE 2 — A HAPPY MEMORY

TIME: 5–10 SECONDS

The camera slowly moves toward the old photograph.

The photograph fills the screen, and its image gradually transforms into a living, animated memory.

Suddenly, we are transported to autumn 1998.

A beautiful young Korean woman stands beneath a magnificent maple tree in a peaceful university garden. Golden leaves float around her as a gentle breeze moves her long black hair.

She wears her cream wool coat and the deep-red knitted scarf.

Her exceptionally handsome boyfriend approaches, carrying a small paper bag from an old-fashioned Korean bakery.

He smiles shyly and gently adjusts the scarf around her neck.

She looks up at him and laughs softly.

He brushes a loose strand of hair away from her face. They exchange a warm, affectionate smile.

Their expressions should communicate the excitement and tenderness of young love.

VISUAL EFFECT: A dreamy, softly glowing atmosphere with delicate floating leaves, gentle sunlight filtering through the maple canopy, subtle depth of field, and beautifully rendered autumn colors.

The memory should feel warm, happy, and precious, as though the elderly woman is reliving her favorite moment.

CAMERA: Gentle tracking movement, intimate close-ups, and graceful transitions between their expressions.

SCENE 3 — THEIR LITTLE WORLD

TIME: 10–15 SECONDS

The young couple walks along an old stone pathway covered in colorful fallen maple leaves.

The young man playfully steps on a dry leaf, making it crackle.

The woman laughs and lightly taps his arm.

He reaches for her hand. Their fingers gently interlock.

title: THE HARVEST KING — SEEDANCE 2.5 DIRECTIVE: Exactly 30 seconds,…
text:
THE HARVEST KING — SEEDANCE 2.5

DIRECTIVE: Exactly 30 seconds, 16:9, photorealistic Hollywood folk-horror, 60fps where supported. Preserve @image1’s exact face, hair, skin tone, build, outfit and props in every shot. No identity drift, clones or costume changes.

LOCATION: Haunted pumpkin farm on Halloween night, foggy field, corn maze on the left, weathered red barn far right, rusted tractor, blue moonlight and glowing orange pumpkins. Maintain geography.

MONSTER: A 15-meter Harvest King made of vines, rotten pumpkins, tractor wheels and farm tools. Giant carved pumpkin head, burning candle inside its mouth (weak point), enormous rusted scythe. Supporting enemies: burlap scarecrows with ember eyes, stitched mouths and rusted sickles.

WEAPON: @image1’s existing equipment plus one rusted iron lantern-hook pole pulled from a fence. Grounded, weighty combat and realistic physics.

TIMELINE:

00:00–00:05 | THE AWAKENING: Macro jack-o’-lantern candle sputters. Crane shot reveals the foggy field as orange light ignites pumpkins toward the barn. @image1 turns toward the glow, alert.

00:05–00:10 | SCARECROWS: Scarecrows break free and attack. The hero tears a rusted iron pole from the fence, dodges a sickle and strikes an attacker into the others. Track laterally through corn.

00:10–00:15 | CROW STORM: Five scarecrows rush him. He blocks sickles, hooks a leg and counters. One powerful boot strike shatters a scarecrow into straw and exploding crows during a 180° slow-motion orbit. Music abruptly fades.

00:15–00:20 | THE GIANT RISES: Earth splits; pumpkins roll inward. The colossal Harvest King erupts from the soil, towering over the barn. It swings its scythe; the hero slides underneath as the blade splinters the fence and barn wall permanently.

00:20–00:25 | THE CLIMB: The hero sprints, leaps onto the embedded scythe handle and climbs onto the giant’s arm. He hooks whipping vines with his pole, swings past them and reaches the shoulder, facing the burning candle inside its mouth.

00:25–00:30 | FINAL TWIST: Flame-lit close-up. He drives the pole through the carved mouth, smashing the candle. A fiery blast erupts; he leaps clear. The giant collapses into rotten pumpkins and straw in slow motion. At dawn, the hero rises among motionless scarecrows. At 00:29.5, the untouched jack-o’-lantern relights and its smile widens. Cut to black at exactly 00:30.

AUDIO: Original score: eerie cello and music box, crows, wind, creaking wood, taiko and choir escalating into 140-BPM orchestral action. Synchronize impacts, metallic scythe whistle, flame blast and giant collapse. Absolute silence at 00:28.5; one final music-box note. No dialogue, text or logos. Maintain continuity of damage, fire, debris and character identity.

Everyone's posting animations made with Opus 5.5. The one quoted below is the most useful I've seen: a designer who struggled to explain their UX decisions in interviews turned them into an animation with Opus 5.5, 𝗼𝗻𝗲 "𝘄𝗵𝘆" 𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽.

Send this prompt to Claude Code to turn one technical decision in your project into an animation like this 👇

"Turn one technical decision in this project into a roughly 40-second blueprint-style explainer animation: each step circles the problem first, turns the screen into a blueprint, moves only what changes, then ends on one line about why we chose it.

1. Read the recent commits and the related code, list 3 decisions worth explaining, and let me pick one.
2. Once I pick, split it into 3 to 5 steps, following problem → options we considered → trade-offs → final choice, one sentence per step. Show me the storyboard first.
3. After I confirm, build it with HyperFrames (if it isn't installed, set it up from http://hyperframes.dev). Use code snippets and architecture diagrams, and make it readable on a phone: keep only the key lines of code and use large text. Cut straight between steps, no black screens. Render it as an MP4.
4. After rendering, grab one frame per second into a contact sheet and check it yourself: no overlapping text, every step clear, and the visuals match what the code actually does. Fix what you find, then show me."

title: Interactive tropical island railway diorama with underwater cutaway
text:
Create a polished, fully interactive 3D artwork called “Pelagia - The Ocean Line” using Three.js and WebGL. Deliver the complete experience in one standalone HTML file that opens directly in Chrome. Build the scene, interactions, animations and audio, not just a mockup.

CONCEPT AND ART DIRECTION

A miniature tropical island with a railway that travels above and below the ocean. Present the island and surrounding water as a large, rounded, elliptical diorama with a transparent water cutaway. The viewer should see the coastal village above the surface and a living underwater world below it simultaneously.

Use a richly detailed miniature aesthetic: turquoise water, pale sand, layered stone, lush palms, cream buildings, terracotta roofs and a vintage red-and-cream train. Aim for a finished interactive artwork with thoughtful composition, soft shadows and inviting lighting.

ISLAND AND TERRAIN

Build a continuous solid terrain volume, from the bedrock base to the shoreline. Show visible geological layers along the cut edge. Fill the space beneath the land completely, without floating surfaces or unexplained cavities.

Include a coastal station with a clock, striped awning, benches, luggage and platform lamps. Add cottages, a striped lighthouse, palm trees, rocks, beach vegetation and small decorative details. All structures and plants must sit correctly on the terrain.

RAILWAY AND UNDERWATER TUNNEL

Create a continuous closed railway route. The train leaves the station, follows the shoreline, crosses a supported viaduct, gradually descends into a transparent underwater tunnel, passes through the reef and returns to the station.

title: Interactive miniature town where typed commands change the world
text:
# Build an Interactive World Model Playground

Build a complete, working browser experience called **Small World**.

It is a beautifully rendered miniature town that people can change through natural language and direct interaction. The world responds through connected systems: pedestrians, traffic, weather, destinations, water, and lighting.

The central experience:

**Change one thing. Watch everything react.**

Act as the product designer, creative coder, simulation engineer, and art director. Make implementation decisions independently within the constraints below.

Implement the experience in the current environment. This is a request for functioning software, not a proposal, mockup, video, or implementation plan.

## 1. The creative premise

Imagine a meticulously designed architectural model that has come alive.

Tiny people have destinations. Cars travel between neighborhoods. A river passes through town. Bridges connect its banks. People visit the park and gather in the square.

Then the user types:

> “Start a festival in the park.”

A small stage and lights appear. People change destinations and begin converging on the park. Nearby paths become busier.

The user continues:

> “Now make it rain.”

Cloud shadows move across the town. Rain begins. Umbrellas appear. Festival visitors leave exposed areas and walk toward reachable shelters.

Then:

> “Close the north bridge.”

Barriers appear. Approaching vehicles stop and choose another route. Pedestrians change their paths. The longer crossing becomes busier.

**These are not separate visual effects. They are consequences unfolding inside the same persistent world.**

That connected behavior is the product.

The experience should be compelling as a silent screen recording, but remain genuinely interactive when someone uses it themselves.

## 2. Priorities and scope

Build one small, exceptionally polished world rather than a sprawling, incomplete city builder.

Prioritize, in this order:

1. A visually distinctive, living miniature.
2. Real, legible cause and effect.
3. Reliable language commands and direct interaction.
4. Smooth motion and immediate feedback.
5. A reproducible showcase sequence.

The required scope is one town and the six interventions described below.

Do not add accounts, multiplayer, a large procedural map generator, economic systems, extensive dashboards, or a general-purpose construction editor.

The town should feel like a carefully composed physical diorama, not a generic low-poly asset pack.

Create a compact landscape with:

- A river separating two neighborhoods.
- Two bridges, with visibly different alternative routes.
- Approximately 12–20 buildings with varied silhouettes.
- A park, a small market square, and a riverside parking lot.

Create a beautiful, interactive 3D gummy citrus slice using WebGPU. Deliver the complete experience in one standalone HTML file with embedded JavaScript and WGSL shaders.

This must be a real-time 3D simulation, not a video, image, or looping animation.

APPEARANCE

Create a thick, semicircular orange slice with translucent, juicy flesh, eight distinct segments, delicate internal membranes, tiny bubbles, a pale pith layer, and a soft orange rind.

Make it look like premium gummy candy: saturated color, glossy highlights, light passing through the flesh, convincing refraction, and soft contact shadows. Avoid excessive bloom, washed-out colors, or a hard plastic appearance.

Use a warm, light studio background and a clean editorial interface with generous whitespace. Add the large italic serif title “Citrus Jelly.” Keep controls compact and the slice clearly visible.

SOFT-BODY PHYSICS

The jelly feel is the most important part.

- Grab any part of the slice with a mouse or finger.
- Pull, lift, stretch, twist, and release it.
- Make deformation local: pulling one edge should stretch nearby flesh while the rest follows naturally.
- After release, the slice should wobble, overshoot, and gradually recover its original shape.
- Include gravity, inertia, damping, ground collisions, and soft bouncing.
- Preserve volume approximately and prevent the mesh from collapsing or turning inside out.
- Make the rind slightly firmer than the flesh.
- Internal segments, membranes, and bubbles must follow the deformation without floating outside the body.

Use a stable volumetric soft-body solver, such as a tetrahedral mesh with XPBD constraints. Do not imitate softness by scaling or rotating the entire object.

CONTROLS

Include three color presets: Orange, Lemon, and Ruby.

Add:
- Firmness slider.
- Internal damping slider.
- “Give it a nudge” button.
- Reset button.
- Quarter-speed checkbox.
- Show mesh checkbox.
- Pause/resume button.

Display small live readouts for mass, percentage of rest volume, and kinetic energy.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

Use genuine WebGPU rendering with WGSL shaders. Generate all geometry and visual details procedurally, without imported models or image files.

Keep simulation updates independent of rendering frame rate. Support desktop and touch devices. Show a clear fallback message if WebGPU is unavailable.

Test strong dragging, repeated releases, all controls, and narrow screens. Fix unstable physics, broken geometry, and visual artifacts before delivering the finished HTML.

The result should feel like a tiny, tactile candy experiment that is genuinely satisfying to play with.

title: One-file looping UI motion design reel with morphing components
text:
<inputs>
Ask me for: 8 to 12 UI states I want the shape to become (e.g. button, loader, player, slider, toggle, tabs, chart, command palette, toast), pure black and white or one accent color, and a royalty-free song around 120 BPM (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Dribbble-level UI motion. One shape, never cut: every state is the same element morphing its size, radius and color while its content swaps with a short blur. A cursor drives every change with real clicks and drags. Light warm-gray canvas, black and white components, one clean UI font (Geist). Springs everywhere, a tiny overshoot at most. The camera zooms so each state fills the frame. The last frame is the first frame, so it loops.
Banned: bouncy easing, particle bursts, glows, gradients on UI chrome, mismatched icon strokes, dead time, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 7 bars, something happens on every beat.
Button → loader → check → dynamic island → music player with a play/pause morph → scrub the progress bar → it becomes a volume slider that stretches when dragged past max → a toggle flips on the beat → the knob becomes a liquid tab indicator → the tabs open into a chart that draws itself, with a tooltip on hover → it collapses into ⌘K → type to filter → enter → toast → back to the button.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, square 1440x1440. Every style is computed from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no state carried between frames.
2. Springs are closed-form step responses. A value that changes target many times is the sum of one spring per change, so it stays a pure function of time.
3. The tab indicator's two edges ride different springs, so the leading edge stretches ahead of the trailing one. Same trick for the toggle knob.
4. Drags are direct manipulation: while the cursor is held, the value is computed from its position. On release it springs back from wherever it was.
5. Analyze the song with numpy for the beat grid and start on a downbeat. Place every UI sound by its measured peak.
6. Render with Playwright: 4 subframes per frame, blended with ffmpeg tmix for motion blur at 60fps.
7. Render one frame per beat before the full render. Fix anything off the grid, cramped or hard to read.
</build>

<gotchas>
Never put will-change on anything the camera scales or the text renders blurry. Text that swaps inside a morphing container needs its own enter and exit timing or it overlaps. Make the last frame identical to the first, cursor position and speed included, or the loop stutters.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the state list on the beat grid before you write any code.

Users can grab the flesh with a mouse or finger, stretch it, and release it.
Deformation should concentrate around the grabbed point rather than simply translating the entire object.
After release, the fruit should wobble, jiggle, and gradually recover its original shape.
Make the peel petals individually draggable. They should be softer than the flesh, bending and springing back while remaining attached to the fruit.

Density badge: ρ 1.04 g/cm³.

Live readouts for mass, percentage of rest volume, and kinetic energy.

A collapsible “Inside the experiment” section explaining the implementation accurately.
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Deliver one self-contained file named pitaya-jelly-webgpu.html.

Use actual WebGPU rendering, not a Canvas 2D imitation.

Build all geometry procedurally.
Use thickness-aware refraction, Fresnel reflections, and soft studio lighting.

title: Browser sandbox game in Minecraft style with survival systems
text: Build a browser sandbox game in the spirit of Minecraft that feels as close to the original as possible. All in-game text in English. Controls: keyboard and mouse (desktop).  TECH - A single HTML file, plain WebGL2, no third-party libraries. - All 16×16 textures generated in code as pixel art (stone, dirt, grass, planks, leaves, ores, glass, water, lava, etc.). - Sounds synthesized with WebAudio: digging, footsteps, placing blocks, damage, mobs, explosions, calm background music.  WORLD - Infinite world made of 16×16×128 chunks, with a seed. - Biomes: plains, forest, birch forest, taiga, snowy tundra, desert, mountains, oceans, beaches. - Caves (winding tunnels and large caverns), lava at the lower levels, ores by depth: coal, iron, gold, diamonds. - Three tree types, tall grass, flowers, cacti, sugar cane, pumpkins. - Minecraft-style lighting: sky light and block light (torches, glowstone, lava) that spreads cell by cell, with smooth lighting and ambient occlusion. - Day/night cycle: sun, moon, stars, sunsets, 3D clouds, distance fog, rain. - Water and lava flow by levels; two sources make infinite water; water + lava make obsidian or cobblestone. Sand and gravel fall.  PLAYER - First person, collisions, jumping, sprinting, sneaking (doesn't fall off edges), swimming, ladders, fall damage. - Block breaking with crack stages and particles; break time depends on the tool. - Visible hand and held item with a swing animation. Third-person view on F5.  SURVIVAL - Health, hunger, saturation, air underwater. - Tools in 5 materials with durability, armor in 4 materials. - Inventory with 2×2 crafting, 3×3 crafting table, furnace with fuel, chests, bed (skip the night and set spawn). - Item drops, death and respawn. - Mobs: pigs, cows, sheep, chickens (breeding, shearing); at night zombies, skeletons with bows, spiders. Zombies and skeletons burn in sunlight. - Farming: hoe, seeds, wheat growth, bread. Doors, fences, fence gates, TNT.  CREATIVE - Flying on double-tap Space, instant block breaking, a catalog of all blocks with tabs and search.  UI - Title screen with a world panorama, world list (create / delete / play), options (FOV, render distance, sensitivity, sound, brightness, GUI scale). - Pause menu, death screen, HUD (hotbar, hearts, hunger, armor, air bubbles), F3 debug screen. - Chat with commands: /gamemode, /time, /give, /tp, /summon, /weather. - Worlds saved in localStorage.  RESTRICTIONS - Do not use Minecraft's name, logo, textures or characters (Steve, Creeper, etc.): give the game its own name and design your own mobs.  TESTING - Run the game in a headless browser, check every system and fix bugs before delivering.

title: Interactive 3D jelly fig in a standalone HTML file
text:
Create an interactive 3D jelly fig half in a single standalone HTML file using genuine WebGPU rendering and WGSL shaders. This must not be an image or a prerecorded animation: the object must respond to user interaction in real time.
Appearance:
A large, ripe fig half with a pear-shaped silhouette, a rounded base, and a slightly elongated tip.

Deep purple skin, a thin pale inner layer, and rich pink-red flesh.
Hundreds of tiny golden seeds, delicate fibers, and translucent jelly structures across the cut surface.
Seeds must have real 3D geometry, not be painted onto the model.
The back must feature a fully modeled, rounded skin. No empty surfaces or holes.
Wet gloss, soft highlights, light refraction, and thickness-dependent transparency. Preserve saturated colors without washed-out white highlights.
The most important part is convincing jelly physics:
The user can grab any part of the fig with a mouse or finger, stretch it, lift it, and release it. The geometry itself must deform: the grabbed area stretches locally, neighboring flesh follows, and the rest of the body retains weight and resistance.
Use a volumetric soft-body simulation, such as a tetrahedral mesh with XPBD elasticity and volume-preservation constraints. Do not substitute whole-object scaling or a uniform sine-wave animation for real deformation.
The skin, flesh, and seeds must move together without lagging behind or clipping through one another. After release, the fig should rebound softly, wobble a few times, and gradually settle. No instant snapping back and no endless oscillation.
Include gravity, inertia, ground contact, and a soft contact shadow. Keep the simulation stable during rapid movements and strong pulls.
Presentation:
A bright studio setting with a warm neutral background and generous whitespace. Place a large italic serif heading, “Fig Jelly.”, on the left, with the caption “A little sweetness. A little surrender.” Position the model in the center and a compact “THE SPECIMEN” panel on the right.
Controls:

Three color presets: Violet, Honey, and Rose.
Firmness and Internal damping sliders.
Give it a nudge, Reset, and Pause buttons.
¼ speed and Show mesh toggles.
A small interaction hint: “Pinch. Pull. Let go.”
Technical requirements:
Keep all code, geometry, and materials inside one HTML file. No external 3D models or texture assets. Support mouse, touch, and different screen sizes. Display a clear fallback message when WebGPU is unavailable.
Verify startup, dragging, release, reset, and parameter changes. Avoid excessive memory allocations in the animation loop.
The final result should feel like a premium interactive gummy dessert: juicy, dimensional, detailed, and so satisfyingly soft that you want to keep squishing it.

title: 7.5-second prompt-to-website reveal for a meme-tech landing page
text:
<inputs>
Ask me for: the product the landing page is for, the prompt a user types, a hero photo for the page, a background photo behind the prompt box, and my model name for the label. If I skip any, use the defaults: a meme landing page "Monke" for a monkey who takes selfies, the famous public-domain monkey selfie from Wikimedia Commons as the hero, the CC0 "Baby goat jumping" photo from Wikimedia Commons as the background (mirrored so the goat leaps on the right), the model label "Opus 5.5", and Mixkit's free track "Voxscape".
</inputs>

<direction>
A 7.5 second prompt-to-website reveal, 1920x1080 at 30fps (226 frames), one continuous take: a prompt types, the send button is pressed, and the box itself becomes the finished landing page.
Look: blue-graded sky #294376→#769cc2 with thin white line graphics (two circles, two horizontal and two vertical lines, two diagonals, 4-point sparkles at the crossings, a blurred violet→yellow→teal rainbow glow top-right, light film grain). The background subject is a crisp, opaque, full-colour cut-out (hand-traced mask, 2–3 px feather) on the right. White prompt box, radius 18, soft shadow; Inter 34.8px/44.4px #121212; black send button with a white arrow; a grey "Opus 5.5 ⌄" label beside it. Freshly typed characters arrive indigo #24249a, pass through blue and maroon, and settle to #121212 over ~13 frames.
Page: full-bleed hero with the subject cut out on the right over a steel-blue sky #3b5876→#75a2c4, and a horizontal motion-blur smear of the subject trailing left. White Inter UI: logo top-left, nav Features/Pricing/FAQ/Download, an outline pill top-right, bold 63px headline, 23px paragraph, white pill CTA, three muted feature rows with icons, three muted wordmarks bottom-left.
Default page copy: logo "Monke"; pill "Made with Claude Opus 5.5"; headline "Smile Harder. Selfie / Smarter, Week by Week"; paragraph "Monke tracks grins, bananas, selfies and naps—then turns every photo into clear, motivating progress you'll actually feel."; CTA "Get the Banana"; features "Grin zones (Z1–Z5 time & trends)", "Banana scores (coach-ready)", "Auto-sync from any camera you steal"; wordmarks BANANA CO. / JUNGLE / OPUS 5.5. Give the monkey white shield sport sunglasses with a mirrored lens (yellow→orange→red→magenta→orange→yellow, vertical streaks, top highlight, drop shadow) along his eye line (25° tilt).
Banned: crossfades between scenes, stock UI kits, glows on the text, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
Default prompt typed: "Build a premium, modern meme-tech landing page for a monkey who takes selfies. Create a full-screen cinematic hero featuring a grinning macaque in sport sunglasses, positioned on the right side with generous negative space on the left. Use a bold white headline about taking better selfies, a short supporting paragraph, and a clean rounded "Get the Banana" CTA. / Add a minimal top navigation with logo."
f0–29, type: the box starts at x884 y635 709x112 and eases out to x570 y477 778x130 (90% there by f12) while the whole scene pulls back 7%. Typing starts on f4 with a real keystroke rhythm, reaches 30 characters by f26, then stalls. Four white selection handles hug the box corners.
f29–44, charge: a violet solarised wash floods the scene (peak f36). The box tilts back up to 12° (rotateX, peak f36), the handles fly out to the frame corners, and an ASCII field of % @ # ⨸ glyphs appears at the left and right edges. The box grows to a tall card x541–1374, y425→227. On f40–48 the rest of the prompt bursts in (about 50 characters per frame) and fills ~12 lines.
f48–63, settle: the tall card lands at x575 y227 766x626. The camera eases back toward the subject. A black cursor appears on f55 at (1455,595), pointing up-left, and grows to 112 px.
f64–96, press: hard cut to a 3.19x zoom on the send button (75 px becomes 239 px on screen), a pale pink wash across the top. The cursor swings in from the right (f64–68) and glides to the button (f68–80). Press f80–86: the cursor squashes to 0.9, the button inflates 12% and flashes Claude terracotta #D97757, and the box edge bulges under it. f93–96 the frame blurs 6 px under a lavender veil.
f97–120, reveal: wide shot. The page's hero photo zooms slowly behind (1.1% per frame). The box (763x596) drops from y60 to y245 with an ease-out, settled by f110. On f106–110 it turns grey, then goes dark from the bottom while a cyan band sweeps down through it (f111–121), wiping the text away.
f121–145, morph: the box grows into the page, from x576 y245 763x596 to full frame on a fast ease-out (half the distance by f127, full by f145). Its fill is glass: a dark veil at the top, a cyan→white band sweeping down and out, white fading away. Every page element slides from inside the box to its final place on one progress curve (50% at f130, 90% at f147, done at f161). The headline types two lines at once from f122 to f158.
f161–224, pull back: the page shrinks around its centre onto a flat #dddddd background, from 1920 px wide to 1344 px (1634 by f173, 1404 by f190, 1344 by f214). The hero's motion blur strengthens as it goes. f225 is black.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, 1920x1080, rendered from seek(t). Every style is a pure function of the frame: no CSS transitions, no timers, no Math.random. Use seeded hashes.
2. Animate with keyframe tables, kf(frame, [[f, value], ...], ease), interpolating numbers or arrays. Every move above is a table of these keyframes.
3. Cut-outs are SVG masks from hand-traced polygons with a 2–3 px Gaussian feather. The motion-blur smear is a scaleX-stretched copy through an SVG horizontal blur (feGaussianBlur stdDeviation="40 0").
4. The press, the grey-to-dark box and the glass card are layered linear gradients whose stop positions are driven by the band value.
5. Sound: no voice.
   - Music: cut Voxscape so its first bass step lands at 1.72 s (source 38.76 s) and its big bass attack at 4.11 s (source 47.36 s, splice at 3.41 s).
   - Low-pass sweeps: the music dips to 400 Hz from 2.4 to 2.78 s and to 150 Hz from 3.41 to 3.58 s, reopens by 4.08, and fades out 6.6–7.5 s.
   - Synthesized sound effects: keystroke ticks on the typing (0.13–1.97 s) and on the headline (4.3–5.1 s); whooshes at 1.35, 2.18 and 3.30 s; a click at 2.78 s; a shimmer rising to 4.08 s; a sub boom at 4.09 s; a pop at 5.15 s; a settle at 6.54 s.
   - Master to -14 LUFS, true peak -1 dBTP.
6. Render with Playwright, one screenshot per frame, then encode h264 at 30 fps and mux the audio.
</build>
